independent_evidence.reason: IUPAC defines an osmometer as an instrument measuring osmotic pressure, and an independent APA dictionary gives the same definition. The exact osmo- plus -meter compound establishes the osmosis-related sense rather than merely the Greek historical root push.

The Association of Migraine Disorders defines osmophobia as fear or aversion to odors; an independent medical review likewise describes intolerance of smells. The exact osmo- plus -phobia formation establishes smell as distinct from osmosis.

A contemporary chemical discussion explicitly analyzes oxi- as the prefix referring to oxide in oximuriate, and another independent period scientific article repeatedly uses oximuriatic gas. The historical spelling oxi- is an obsolete chemical variant of oxy-; the old terminology does not imply chlorine contains oxygen.

The Smithsonian describes paleoart as art reconstructing prehistoric life informed by paleontological evidence; the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles likewise treats paleoart as reconstructions based on fossil research. The word is paleo- for paleontology plus art, giving the exact claimed specialized sense.

A United Nations report describes Papuo-Melanesians among Papua inhabitants, while Australian National University research identifies Papuo-Melanesian as New Guinea Melanesian languages, documenting a historical combination of Papua-related and Melanesian elements. The exact Papuo- plus Melanesian is attested; the historical categories reflect period terminology.

Oxford defines pedturbation as soil mixing and explicitly gives it as a variant of pedoturbation; an independent geography department publication also uses the exact English term for soil mixing. The exact ped- plus turbation illustrates the soil sense. Existing independently established ped- child and foot senses remain intact.

Wolfram and a Johns Hopkins mathematical study describe the attested term pentakis dodecahedron with 60 triangular faces, five for each of the 12 dodecahedron faces; the mathematical modifier pentakis means five times and combines with the numerical dodecahedron. This is the mathematical multiplication sense, separate from the already accepted chemical substituent sense.

Dictionary.com cites the adjective Anglophobiac modifying clergyman and defines its base Anglophobia as aversion or hostility toward England or English people; the original lexical source independently lists the same adjectival form for dislike. The exact suffix -phobiac forms the requested aversion adjective.

Collins defines Anglophobiac as a person with fear or dread of England or the English, and an independent historical congressional speech uses an Anglophobiac as a noun. Anglo- plus -phobiac therefore names a person experiencing the specified phobia.

An inorganic chemistry textbook defines phosphonitrile compounds by their phosphorus–nitrogen bonds and gives examples without oxygen or phosphate; an independent chemical nomenclature paper identifies the PN group as the phosphonitrile radical. Thus phospho- here denotes phosphorus rather than phosphate. The earlier phosphate example phospholipid remains accepted.

A historical JAMA article uses phthisiotherapy explicitly for a branch of tuberculosis treatment, and an independent history of tuberculosis identifies it with sanatorium therapy. The exact phthisio- plus therapy means treatment of phthisis, resolving the earlier concern that translated titles alone did not show English use.

A marine ecology review defines picoplankton as 0.2–2 micrometres, below nanoplankton and microplankton; an independent University of Hawaii-hosted study uses the same conventional class. The exact pico- plus plankton reflects this biological size class rather than the SI factor 10^-12.

The WHO international nonproprietary-name stem guide defines -pin(e) for tricyclic compounds and lists clozapine in that group. FDA independently identifies clozapine as a tricyclic dibenzodiazepine. The exact drug-name ending -pine therefore has the proposed chemical class meaning, unrelated to the tree noun pine.

A historical scientific dictionary defines plastogamy as union involving fusion of cytoplasm without nuclei; a separate university-hosted embryology text describes plastogamy as fusion of plasmas. Thus exact plasto- plus -gamy refers to cytoplasm and union, independently of the prior plasticity sense.

Merriam-Webster lists plastochron for formation or development; an independent botanical review defines it as the interval between successive leaf primordium initiation events. The exact plasto- plus chron denotes time in formation or development. The previously accepted plasticity example remains intact.

Canada’s terminology bank defines plastogene as a genetic locus associated with a plant plastid, and an independent plant-biology dictionary describes it as a gene attached to a plastid. Exact plasto- plus gene therefore establishes the plastid sense; existing plasticity examples remain.

WHO lists brodimoprim among antibacterial trimethoprim derivatives using the -prim stem; the IUPHAR/BPS guide independently describes brodimoprim as a trimethoprim analogue inhibiting bacterial dihydrofolate reductase. Its exact final -prim illustrates the requested pharmaceutical naming element.

Exact pudendo- plus anal refers to the external genital and anal reflex pathway.

Hashimi is used in English-language scholarship for affiliation with the Banu Hashim clan; an Arabic nomenclature study explicitly derives Hashimi from the name Hashim using the nisba suffix -i.
An etymological dictionary traces millionaire to French million plus -aire; Webster independently defines the exact word as one whose wealth amounts to millions.
Etymonline and Oxford independently trace alphanumeric to a blend of alphabet and numeric; alpha- is the clipped alphabetic component rather than the first-letter sense.
The US National Weather Service identifies alto- as the middle cloud level and altocumulus as its example; Oxford independently traces the exact term to alto plus cumulus.
A medical terminology reference defines axio- as relating to an axis; Toronto dentistry independently uses axiobuccal in describing the axial and buccal cavity margins.
Dictionary.com derives basiate from Latin basium kiss and -ate, and an independent English etymology dictionary records the same kiss root and derivatives.
Collins identifies biblio- specifically meaning Bible in bibliolatry; an independent dictionary analyzes the word and defines it as reverence for the Bible.
The WHO stem book lists calci for vitamin D analogues and explicitly includes calcipotriol; the British Pharmacological Society independently classifies this exact drug as such an analogue.
A medical dictionary gives cardiotomy as incision of the stomach cardia, and the Canadian terminology bureau independently records that exact surgical sense.
A medical terminology course identifies carp(o) as the wrist; Cambridge independently defines carpometacarpal as relating to the carpus and metacarpus.
The National Museum of Health and Medicine derives causalgia from Greek heat and pain; Cambridge medical history independently records the same coined term and derivation.
Collins distinguishes the cavity suffix -cele from the hernia suffix and gives blastocele; US National Library of Medicine independently defines the exact word as the blastula cavity.
An agricultural microbiology thesis explains -cin bacteriocin naming and gives colicin; a US FDA document independently identifies colicins as bacteriocins.
A scientific affix dictionary defines -clastic as breaking or disintegrating, while Cambridge explains osteoclastic as relating to cells that break down bone.
The Salamanca medical etymology dictionary analyzes colitis as colon plus inflammation, and Etymonline independently confirms the same formation and meaning.
The WHO INN stem book lists cort for corticosteroids and cites cortivazol; the US National Library of Medicine independently classifies cortivazol as a glucocorticoid.
The WHO INN stem book explicitly lists deflazacort under the corticosteroid stem cort, and the US FDA independently identifies it as a corticosteroid prodrug.
The FDA identifies dexmethylphenidate as the d-threo enantiomer of methylphenidate; an independent stereochemistry review explicitly identifies it as the dextrorotatory isomer.
Cambridge defines electropop as pop made with electronic instruments, and an independent dictionary identifies it as electronic pop music.
Dictionary.com analyzes pearlescent as pearl plus -escent, and Wordsmyth independently identifies resembling as a meaning of that suffix with pearlescent as its example.
A botanical glossary defines allogamous as reproducing by cross-fertilization; a plant variety standards document independently uses it for cross-fertilized reproduction.
The Century Dictionary explicitly analyzes alkaligenous as alkali plus -genous producing and defines it as producing alkali; Webster independently confirms the word and meaning.
The WHO INN stem book identifies gli for antihyperglycemic medicines and lists glimepiride; DailyMed independently identifies it as a glucose-lowering sulfonylurea.
Penn State analyzes geography into geo and graphy and defines it as the study of Earth; Etymonline independently derives the term from earth and description.
A CERN physics presentation uses hadrochemistry for hadron abundances, and a University of Turin thesis independently defines it as the study of particle species abundance.
Cambridge and Oxford independently record kilobyte as 1024 bytes in computing, alongside the decimal meaning; this binary usage extends metric kilo.
Etymonline and Oxford University Press independently analyze wedlock as wed plus the historical action suffix, unrelated to the homographic fastening noun.
A historical English dictionary identifies philologue as philologist, and Oxford historical lexicography independently lists philologue among expert nouns in -logue.
A University of Granada dissertation analyzes meloplasty as cheek plus surgical repair, and an independent medical dictionary confirms the cheek-reconstruction meaning.
The University of Virginia identifies met- as a form of meta meaning after, and an independent university medical terminology guide identifies metencephalon as afterbrain.
Cambridge and the Oxford Dictionary of Music independently define metallophone as an instrument sounding through metal bars; this is the metal sense rather than mine.
Collins defines narco-state in terms of a state and illicit narcotics trade; an independent peer-reviewed article discusses the same drug-trade label.
Etymonline identifies plugola as a covert promotional practice involving a bribe; an independent broadcast dictionary confirms promotion in exchange for merchandise.
American Heritage analyzes crapola as crap plus -ola and defines it as nonsense; Collins independently describes the same suffix as forming jocular variations.
Etymonline analyzes trachoma from Greek roughness plus -oma, while the World Health Organization independently identifies trachoma as an eye disease.
The World Health Organization lists -orphan for opioid morphinan derivatives including levomethorphan; an independent pharmacology review identifies the same compound as a morphinan opioid.
The US Centers for Disease Control and Merck independently define leukocytosis as an increased number of white blood cells, rather than their normal condition.
Khan Academy and an independent cell biology research review both describe phagocytosis as the process of cellular engulfment.
The New York Botanical Garden defines paripinnate leaves as having an even number of leaflets; the Smithsonian independently identifies the same even-pinnate form.
A college Latin primer explains pari- as equal in parisyllabic, and an independent historical dictionary traces the word to equal plus syllable.
Etymonline traces pedometer to Latin foot and Greek measure; an independent historical dictionary describes it as a device registering footsteps.
Etymonline traces pedology to Greek pedon ground and -logy; Colorado State University independently explains the same soil-science etymology.
Collins traces perchance to Old French par meaning by plus chance; an independent historical Scots dictionary records the same by-chance construction.
Etymonline and an independent chemical history identify peroxide as originally named for the greatest oxygen proportion; modern peroxide nomenclature differs.
A Hong Kong fisheries reference describes physoclist fish by their closed swim bladder; an independent lexical entry segments the same term as physo plus closed.
IUPAC describes cytoplasm as the material within a cell surrounding its organelles; Oxford independently defines it as cellular material excluding the nucleus.
Etymonline derives Singapore from Sanskrit lion plus city, and an independent national museum guide explains its related Singapura name as Lion City.
A dermatology pharmacology study identifies prednicarbate as a prednisolone derivative; an independent chemical database confirms the same drug relationship.
An analytical pharmacology article identifies amisulpride as chemically related to sulpiride; DrugCentral independently lists it among sulpiride derivatives and analogues.
The National Cancer Institute defines pyelitis as inflammation of the renal pelvis; an independent medical etymology reference identifies pyel as basin or renal pelvis.
Merriam-Webster defines the chemical combining form spiro- for rings sharing one atom, while Imperial College independently describes the exact term spiroaromatic in that sense.
Spirochete derives from Greek speira coil and khaite hair; Etymonline and Collins independently support this form and separate it from Latin spirare to breathe.
Popestock is a documented nickname for a papal youth festival by analogy with Woodstock; linguistic commentary independently identifies -stock as a festival-forming element.
Dictionary.com documents libtard as a derogatory blend of liberal and retard; Macquarie independently identifies the productive pejorative suffix -tard.
Samsung and Dell document the historical computer usage of terabyte as 2 to the 40 bytes; it is context-dependent and distinct from the standard decimal SI meaning.
Oxford identifies -th as a noun suffix denoting action or process, and Etymonline independently derives growth from the verb grow plus -th.
Sunderland City Council traces Washington to an Old English settlement name and identifies -ton as settlement; the Society for Name Studies independently documents the place-name element.
The historical Oxford entry describes trachelomastoid as a neck-to-mastoid muscle, and an independent anatomy text places the muscle in the neck and identifies its mastoid insertion.
Collins defines the numeral-forming -ty as multiplication by ten; linguistic research independently analyzes forty as four combined with this historical numeric element.
A linguistic study explicitly lists uber-fan with the meaning number-one fan, while Cambridge independently identifies uber- as a prefix denoting an extreme example.
Oxford identifies ur- as earliest or original and uses urtext; Cambridge independently explains the exact word as original plus text from German.
The mineral society explains uranocircite as named for uranium and Falkenstein, and the independent mineralogical handbook corroborates the same name and composition.
IEEE Spectrum identifies -verse as a clipped universe suffix denoting a sphere and explicitly gives Twitterverse; an independent linguistic paper analyzes Twitter plus universe.
Mirrorverse names an alternate fictional universe; independent game journalism explicitly describes the Mirrorverse as an alternate or divergent Disney universe.
The University of Vienna fandom study identifies -verse as the fictional universe of a fandom; a Star Trek commentary independently uses Trekverse to denote that fictional world.
WHO identifies vir as an antiviral naming stem and published antiviral research independently identifies carbovir as a virus inhibitor, with vir at the end of the drug name.

Merriam-Webster groups akro- as a variant of acro- and supplies height among the combining form senses; an independent English medical book uses the exact spelling akrophobia for dread of heights. The attested form segments akro- plus phobia; preserve the previous akroterion edge.

American Heritage and Collins both analyze English metope through Greek meta meaning between and ope meaning opening; the English spelling preserves the prevocalic met- form, with the following o belonging to ope. They independently define an architectural space between triglyphs.

Collins explicitly segments metempirical as met- plus empirical and defines it as beyond experience. York University's historical psychology dictionary independently records the same word as beyond the range of possible experience and traces it to meta plus experience.

In its statistical sense metanalysis is an attested uncommon spelling of meta-analysis, analysis of prior analyses: BMJ explicitly calls it an elision of meta- with analysis, while a peer-reviewed systematic study uses this spelling for random-effects pooling. This is distinct from the homographic linguistic word meaning resegmentation; retain the statistical sense only.

Collins defines metronymic as a name derived from a mother and traces it to Greek mother plus name; Etymonline independently gives Greek meter, genitive metros, plus onyma. The exact English letters segment metr- plus onymic, with o belonging to the name element.

A historical English dictionary records tobreak as break in pieces; an independent philological study describes historical to- as expressing separation into pieces. The existing tobeat intensive is preserved.
